new_entities.name: Selenium supplementation in Hashimoto thyroiditis
new_entities.description: Selenium supplementation, typically around 200 micrograms daily, used in adults with Hashimoto thyroiditis.

new_entities.name: TPO antibody levels
new_entities.description: The concentration of thyroid peroxidase antibodies, a marker of thyroid autoimmunity in Hashimoto thyroiditis.

edges.effect_quant: A 2024 meta-analysis found selenium lowered TPOAb levels in Hashimoto thyroiditis with SMD -0.96 across 29 cohorts and 2,358 participants. Earlier trials and reviews also suggest antibody lowering, but the literature remains heterogeneous and the clinical importance of changing TPOAb titers is still debated.
edges.population: adults with Hashimoto thyroiditis, with or without thyroid hormone replacement therapy
edges.mechanism: Selenium may reduce oxidative stress within thyroid tissue and modulate immune activity, which can dampen autoimmune thyroid antibody production.
edges.summary: This is one of the cleaner laboratory-effect edges in the thyroid block. Selenium often lowers TPO antibody levels, but that biomarker improvement does not automatically translate into better symptoms or reduced need for thyroid hormone.
edges.caveats: Trial quality is mixed, formulations vary, and antibody lowering may not reflect meaningful clinical benefit. Selenium is also not risk-free at excessive doses, so enthusiasm should stay anchored to measured deficiency risk and realistic outcome goals.

evidence.notes: Selenium Supplementation in Patients with Hashimoto Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.

effect_quant.comparator: TPOAb levels with selenium supplementation versus control across randomized cohorts

evidence.notes: Effect of selenium on thyroid autoimmunity and regulatory T cells in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis: A prospective randomized-controlled trial.

evidence.citation: WintherKH et al 2013 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
